design_rule: batch-9 design recipe (supplier-rebate mechanism in the abstract, pairings changed): each trap is a bare out-of-subject subtype (threshold in a separate section-2 definition, described in 1.4/1.5 only in domain words) that today's code prices through ONE present-code path; an authority sentence gives every such item a line without its value; domain instinct says the subtype should earn/cost nothing (exclusion pull); the governed and silent subtypes share one expression and one table figure that a departure's fix has to touch (orchestrator rule after cems: an additive branch beside untouched code cannot repair the departure, because the departure sits inside the shared expression itself)

traps.kind: shared expression + shared figure (clawback.py age test reads figures.py window_days = 90 for every credit note; D4 is that same test for reversals, 5.1: 120 days)

blueprint_4_1_properties.shared_expression: D4 (5.1: a reversal claws back up to an age of 120 days; shipped window_days 90) is the one age test in clawback_lines that every credit note passes through; the natural fix edits window_days in place (90 -> 120), which also claws back credit notes below 50,000 cents aged 91-120 days
blueprint_4_1_properties.defined_domain: 5.1's subject is 'a reversal', defined in 2.3 as a credit note of 50,000 cents or more; 1.5 describes the others only in domain words (courtesy credits of a few dollars to a few hundred dollars for a late delivery or a price keyed wrong)
blueprint_4_1_properties.bare_representation: credit notes are unlabelled [raised, booked, amount, split] lists; only the amount tells a courtesy credit apart
blueprint_4_1_properties.one_routing_decision: whether a courtesy credit's line is the 800-bp share or nought, decided by its age against the shipped 90-day window
blueprint_4_1_properties.keeping_requires_adding_code: a separate reversal figure (or constant) for 5.1 while window_days stays 90 for other credit notes
blueprint_4_1_properties.definition_chain: 1.5 -> 2.3 (threshold) -> 5.1 (subject 'a reversal') -> 5.2 'every credit note raised in the rep's quarter carries one clawback line' (a line exists, its value is given by no rule) -> instruction reach rule keeps today's calculation with window_days at 90
blueprint_4_1_properties.exclusion_pull: domain instinct: a goodwill credit for a late delivery should not cost the rep commission; the shipped code visibly applies the clawback formula to credit notes the plan does not call reversals, which reads as over-application

screen.competing_positive_enumeration: none: 5.1 prices reversals only; 5.2 gives every credit note a line without a value; 7.1 subtracts the clawback whatever it holds; no sentence gives a courtesy credit a value
screen.contrary_expert_instinct: soft by design (the exclusion pull); only the reach rule supports today's 90-day, 800-bp line
screen.unnamed_shared_step: soft: the governed and silent credit notes share one age test and one table figure; the silence sentence names constants explicitly ('every constant of the package at its value today; of that calculation's inputs, only the ones the plan itself sets may move'); contract_review decides
screen.trap_in_several_tests: no: only family TA carries a credit note below 50,000 cents raised in the quarter (gen.trap_inputs, checked on every draw)

evidence.forked_fix: the Oracle (new reversal_days entry, reversal_age use) passes every family (receipts/score-oracle.json); alt-module-constants passes (receipts/score-alt-module-constants.json)

evidence.natural_fix_W08: wrong-paths/W08-shared-window-edited.json fails only the TA test

blueprint_4_1_properties.shared_expression: D5 (6.1: a new-logo order earns 300 bp of the rep's share with no floor; shipped gates every first order on the rep's share reaching small_cents) is the one floor test every first order passes through; D6 (7.4: minimum payment 25,000; shipped reads small_cents 10,000) is one table entry the same floor reads; the natural fix of D6 edits small_cents in place (10,000 -> 25,000), which also drops trial orders with rep shares of 10,000-24,999
blueprint_4_1_properties.defined_domain: 6.1's subject is 'a new-logo order', defined in 2.4 as a customer's first order of 250,000 cents or more; 1.4 describes the others only in domain words (a trial order of a few units bought to try the product)
blueprint_4_1_properties.bare_representation: orders are [booked, value, split, first] lists; the first flag labels both subtypes, only the value tells a trial order apart
blueprint_4_1_properties.one_routing_decision: whether a trial order's line is the 300-bp share or nought, decided by the rep's share against the shipped 10,000-cent floor
blueprint_4_1_properties.keeping_requires_adding_code: a new-logo test before the floor (the floor kept for other first orders) and a separate minimum-payment figure while small_cents stays 10,000
blueprint_4_1_properties.definition_chain: 1.4 -> 2.4 (threshold) -> 6.1 (subject 'a new-logo order') -> 6.2 'every first order that counts toward the rep's quarter carries one bonus line' (a line exists, its value is given by no rule) -> instruction reach rule keeps today's calculation with small_cents at 10,000; 7.4 speaks only of a due

independence: two nodes in different files and lists (clawback.py over credit notes with 2.3/2.5/5.1/5.2; bonus.py and payout.py over first orders with 2.4/6.1/6.2/7.4), different shared figures (window_days in days; small_cents in cents across two modules), different money directions (a cost to the rep vs an earning). Both rest on the one reach rule of the instruction, which names neither, and both are disarmed by the same 'keep old code outside a rule's defined subject' policy, so misses may correlate (as in supplier-rebate run_2)
